analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 against the replayed patches, file metadata and canonical definition index, including supplied TB-002/TB-011 details. .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml:169 adds the run-scoping request header; head :196-202 passes RUN_ID into jq and appends it after the optional size suffix when constructing expected labels. This narrows the intended CI runner selection rather than changing provider authorization, encryption, attestation, inference, billing or cache controls. No supported regression involving T-053/T-054 or other indexed threats was identified. CI build integrity remains relevant to A-017; a scheduling label is not proof of runner provenance.

changelog.d/ci-run-isolation.md:3 and docs/developer/build.md head :492-501 consistently describe run-specific scheduling and fallback for unsupported responses. The documentation explicitly preserves run identity on individual-job retries, so this does not promise isolation between attempts of the same run. Modes are unchanged for modified files; the new changelog is non-executable.

No concrete vulnerability is established by the supplied changes. However, replay omits three reviewed source units, including surrounding decision validation and fallback behavior; the prior analysis's claims about exact-array matching, GitHub-derived RUN_ID validation and unchanged safety controls cannot all be independently rechecked here. Integration still needs to verify those controls and the external plane/provisioner contract: an accepted response must correspond to registered run-labelled runners that remain available for queued jobs and retries. Missing external implementation is not evidence of a regression, but mismatched provisioning could strand jobs. These remaining coverage and end-to-end availability questions require further review.
